subject: land leech
title: For 700 Years, Nobody Believed Leeches Could Fly at You

scenes.text: Nearly seven hundred years ago, a traveller wrote about flying leeches.
Ibn Battuta described them in what's now Sri Lanka, in the thirteen hundreds.
In 1968, a study said land leeches do not jump onto their prey.
Then, in Madagascar's rainforest, a scientist filmed one coil back on a leaf, like a cobra.
And launch itself through the air. The first proof that a leech can jump.
So the next leech on your leg may not have crawled there.

description:
Since the 1300s, travellers described leeches leaping at people, but scientists dismissed it, and a 1968 study said land leeches do not jump onto prey.
Video filmed in Madagascar in 2017 and 2023 shows the land leech Chtonobdella fallax coiling back like a cobra and jumping, the first conclusive evidence.
Would you go back into that forest?
first_comment: In the 1800s, the biologist Ernst Haeckel also wrote that leeches 'can even spring to reach their victim'. It took until now to catch it on video. What else have scientists dismissed?
